subject.title: fix(streaming): preserve paragraph separators across block-streamed deliveries [AI-assisted]

question: Should the permanent block-streaming contract carry paragraph boundary semantics as in-band text, explicit seam metadata, or an intentionally partial common-case repair?
rationale: The shared layer is the right boundary, but source inspection and contributor discussion show the text-only approach cannot preserve every maxChars boundary without a contract choice.

options.title: Require complete boundary semantics
options.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation that preserves paragraph boundaries for both common and near-limit splits before merge.

options.title: Adopt explicit seam metadata
options.body: Ask the PR authors to carry paragraph/newline/hard-split boundary metadata through chunker, subscriber, and coalescer if in-band text cannot satisfy the invariants.

options.title: Accept a partial repair
options.body: Maintainers may knowingly land the common-case improvement and keep the maxChars edge tracked on the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require complete boundary semantics
recommendation.body: Choose one candidate or replacement implementation that preserves paragraph boundaries for both common and near-limit splits before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has both project-level decision authority from CONTRIBUTING.md and history in the coalescer/chunking surfaces that define the contract.
